headline: New evening confusion reported Nov 15 (including a stove left on) follows a Sep 23 fall and a Nov 5 ED visit for dehydration and dizziness, and the outcome of the planned work-up is not documented.

items.statement: On Nov 15, 2026 her son Marcus reported about two weeks of increased evening confusion, with the stove left on once. The RN found her oriented to person and place but not date, with no fever. Plan was urinalysis, medication review and a PCP visit that week. No results or PCP visit are documented in the notes provided.
items.verifier_note: All details match the Nov 15 nursing note. The statement that no results or PCP visit are documented is a fair observation about the notes provided.

items.statement: On Sep 23, 2026 she had a night-time fall in the bathroom at home and was found on the floor by her son. She denied head strike or loss of consciousness, and no injury was noted. Fall risk was reassessed as high and a PT referral was placed.
items.verifier_note: The Sep 23 nursing note matches every detail: night-time bathroom fall, found by her son, no head strike or LOC, no injury, high fall risk, PT referral.

items.statement: PT evaluation on Oct 1, 2026 found slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommended a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly. Completion of these recommendations is not documented.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation matches on gait, cane use, TUG of 19 seconds, the three recommendations and twice-weekly visits. The statement that completion isn't documented is accurate.

items.statement: On Nov 5, 2026 she was seen in the partner hospital ED for dehydration and dizziness, treated and released the same day, with no new medications. The PCP follow-up on Nov 11 found her back to baseline per her son, with plans to monitor closely for two weeks.
items.verifier_note: The ED discharge summary, the encounter record and the Nov 11 PCP note support every detail: dehydration and dizziness, treated and released the same day, no new medications, back to baseline per her son, and monitoring for two weeks.

questions_for_team: Were the urinalysis, medication review and PCP visit planned on Nov 15 completed, and what did they show?
Could the Nov 5 dehydration and dizziness, the Sep 23 fall and the new evening confusion be related, and who is following this?
What is the status of the front-wheeled walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and is PT continuing twice weekly?
What stove and home-safety supports are needed given the stove left on, and is the family getting caregiver support?
One note (1462f7fa-n013) was withheld by the injection screen because it contained instructions aimed at an AI summarizer. Who will review it?

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: ED visits, urgent care, hospital admissions, observation stays, and any discharges, with reasons.

Falls and near-falls since last review: count, circumstances, injuries, and whether any were reported to the team. Age 85 on antiplatelet therapy, so check specifically for head strikes or bleeding after falls.
Chest pain, angina, or nitroglycerin use: review frequency of nitroglycerin spray use, any new cardiac symptoms, ischemic heart disease events, and cardiology or PCP contacts in the window.

Medication reconciliation: simvastatin appears twice on the active list (10 MG started 2026-08-16 and 20 MG started 2020-07-11). Verify with prescriber and pharmacy whether this is a duplicate, a dose change, or an intended combination; confirm which strength the participant is actually taking and whether the 20 MG entry was discontinued. Flag for prescriber review, not a recommendation to change.

Medication starts and stops in the window beyond the simvastatin entries: confirm metoprolol succinate, clopidogrel, and nitroglycerin are still active and taken as prescribed, and check for any new antithrombotic or NSAID use that could add bleeding risk with clopidogrel.
Bleeding or bruising signs on clopidogrel: nosebleeds, gum bleeding, dark stools, hematuria, unexplained bruising, and any anemia or relevant labs drawn in the window.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend since last review, including orthostatic readings if recorded, given beta-blocker use and fall risk. Note any hypotension or bradycardia documented.
Weight trend and BMI: obesity (BMI 30+) on record. Compare most recent weights to prior review, note change of 5% or more, and check for any nutrition or dietary referral items.

Glycemic status: prediabetes on record. Review most recent A1c or glucose values and any monitoring changes in the window; confirm whether any diabetes medication was started (none is currently listed).
Lipid and cardiovascular labs: review any lipid panel drawn in the window and whether results were reviewed by a prescriber, given hyperlipidemia and the recent statin change.
Breast cancer history (dx 1997): check for any oncology follow-up, surveillance imaging, or new breast symptoms, and confirm survivorship care-plan items are current.
Function and ADLs/IADLs: compare current ADL and IADL status with last review, including transfers, bathing, meal preparation, medication management, and driving or transportation changes.

Cognition and mood: screen results or observations since last review (e.g., cognitive screen, depression screen), changes in memory, confusion, or withdrawal, and any missed or refused PACE center attendance.
Caregiver and social situation: changes in living arrangement, caregiver availability or strain, transportation barriers, food or housing insecurity, and any new supports requested.

PACE attendance and care-plan items due: adult day center attendance pattern in the window, IDT care plan goals and their status, any assessments or reassessments due by the review date 2026-11-30, and outstanding referrals or pending authorizations.
